claims.claim: The temples were cut into 1,036 blocks for relocation
claims.quote: In total the temples were cut into 1,036 blocks.

claims.claim: The temple was cut out of a cliff for Ramesses II from about 1264 BC
claims.quote: Construction of the temple complex started in c. 1264 BC and lasted for about 20 years, until 1244 BC.

claims.claim: The construction work took roughly twenty years
claims.quote: Construction of the temple complex started in c. 1264 BC and lasted for about 20 years, until 1244 BC.

claims.claim: The temple was rebuilt uphill in the 1960s to escape Lake Nasser
claims.quote: The complex was relocated in its entirety in 1968 to higher ground to avoid it being submerged by Lake Nasser, the Aswan Dam reservoir.

claims.claim: The facade image is of the Great Temple, Abu Simbel, by Olaf Tausch, 2019
claims.quote: Description: Great Temple at Abu Simbel, Egypt / Date: 2019-10-25 / Author: Olaf Tausch

claims.claim: By the 6th century BC sand reached the statues' knees
claims.quote: By the 6th century BC, the sand already covered the statues of the main temple up to their knees.

claims.claim: In 1813 Burckhardt saw one head and part of a chest above the sand drift
claims.quote: The entire head, and part of the breast and arms of one of the statues are yet above the surface

claims.claim: Burckhardt found the site in 1813
claims.quote: The temple remained unknown to Europeans until March 1813, when the Swiss researcher Johann Ludwig Burckhardt found the small temple and top frieze of the main temple.

claims.claim: Belzoni's party dug for 22 days and entered the Great Temple on 1 August 1817
claims.quote: After 22 days’ work, he and his party were able to enter the Great Temple on 1 August 1817.

claims.claim: Giovanni Finati, the slenderest of the party, crept through first
claims.quote: I, being one of the slenderest of the party, without a word said, crept through into the interior, and was thus the first that entered it, perhaps, for a thousand years.

claims.claim: The sand-buried colossus photograph is by Francis Frith, 1857, CC0
claims.quote: Date: 1857 ... Author: Francis Frith Licence: CC0

claims.claim: The figure seated on the colossus's crown is a servant posed to provide scale
claims.quote: In a number of photographs, Du Camp had his servant and occasional laboratory assistant Louis Sasseti pose to provide scale.

claims.claim: The servant in the frame was Louis Sasseti
claims.quote: In a number of photographs, Du Camp had his servant and occasional laboratory assistant Louis Sasseti pose to provide scale.

claims.claim: Maxime Du Camp photographed the Great Temple in March 1850
claims.quote: arriving at 9 am on 27 March 1850 and departing on 30 March ... five of the Grand Temple on 29 March

claims.claim: The sun reaches the four sanctuary statues twice a year, on 22 October and 22 February, but Ptah stays dark
claims.quote: on October 22 and February 22, the rays of the sun would penetrate the sanctuary and illuminate the sculptures on the back wall, except for the statue of Ptah, a god connected with the realm of the dead, who always remained in the dark

claims.claim: Ptah is tied to the realm of the dead
claims.quote: except for the statue of Ptah, a god connected with the realm of the dead

claims.claim: The sanctuary of the Great Temple contains four seated statues
claims.quote: Here, on a black wall, are rock cut sculptures of four seated figures: Ra-Horakhty, the deified king Ramesses, and the gods Amun Ra and Ptah.

claims.claim: The sanctuary photograph is by Gary Todd, 2002, CC0
claims.quote: Date: 2002-06-12 06:34 Author: Gary Todd  from Xinzheng, China Licence: CC0

claims.claim: At the Small Temple the queen is carved the same size as the king
claims.quote: Remarkably, this is one of very few instances in Egyptian art where the statues of the king and his consort have equal size.

claims.claim: The Small Temple honours Hathor and Nefertari
claims.quote: The temple of Hathor and Nefertari, also known as the Small Temple, was built about 100 m (330 ft) northeast of the temple of Ramesses II and was dedicated to the goddess Hathor and Ramesses II's chief consort, Nefertari.

claims.claim: Queens were traditionally no taller than the pharaoh's knee
claims.quote: Traditionally, the statues of the queens stood next to those of the pharaoh, but were never taller than his knees.

claims.claim: The Nefertari's Temple photograph dates from 2007
claims.quote: Description: Nefertari's Temple at Abu Simbel. Taken by myself. May 30, 2007. Date: 2007-05-30

claims.claim: The Great Temple was rebuilt 65 metres higher and 208 m further inland
claims.quote: 208 m (682 ft) further inland and vertically 65 m (213 ft) higher for the Great Temple, and 67 m (220 ft) for the Small Temple

claims.claim: The permitted deviation when reassembling the Great Temple was 5 mm
claims.quote: To ensure the correct orientation, the permitted deviation when reassembling the Great Temple was plus or minus 5 mm.

claims.claim: Faces were sawn off from behind the ears
claims.quote: Then on 15 October, the most experienced stone cutters commenced cutting the first face away from behind their ears.

claims.claim: One face weighed 19.6 tonnes
claims.quote: Face weighs 19.6 tonnes and concrete reinforcement in the back of 4.58 tons.

claims.claim: Because the temple was moved, the solar alignment may not be exact
claims.quote: This is compounded by the fact that the temple was relocated from its original setting, so the current alignment may not be as precise as the original one.

claims.claim: The construction/lifting photograph is by Per-Olow Anderson, 1967
claims.quote: Date: 1967 Author: "Per-Olow" - Per-Olow Anderson (1921-1989)

claims.claim: The Aswan High Dam would have raised the water up to 60 metres over the temples
claims.quote: The resulting lake would raise the water level at Abu Simbel by up to 60 metres (200 ft).

claims.claim: Wet sandstone loses its strength
claims.quote: Once submerged the water would cause the sandstone from which they were constructed to lose its strength and durability.

claims.claim: One rescue scheme was to leave the temples underwater behind a dam holding clear filtered water, with visitors viewing from observation galleries
claims.quote: to leave them where they were and building a dam around them, containing crystal-clear filtered water kept at the same height as the muddy Nile water outside. Visitors would then have looked at the engulfed temples from curved observation galleries on three levels.

claims.claim: The viewing galleries in that scheme were to be of glass
claims.quote: Visitors would then have looked at the engulfed temples from curved observation galleries on three levels.

claims.claim: Another scheme proposed floating the temples up on concrete barges
claims.quote: Another scheme proposed by an American construction executive was to construct concrete barges under the temples and then allow the rising lake water to raise them.

claims.claim: The chosen plan of sawing the temples into blocks and rebuilding them uphill was estimated at $36 million, half the cost of the other proposals
claims.quote: was estimated to cost US$36 million, half the cost of the other proposals

claims.claim: The smallest block weighed seven tons
claims.quote: The smallest individual block weighed seven tons.

claims.claim: Crowns were cut off because the heads exceeded the 30-ton lifting limit
claims.quote: As the heads of figures of the pharaohs on the front of the Great Temple exceeded the 30-ton lifting limit, the weight was reduced by cutting their crown off.

claims.claim: The temples were oriented at the new site so the sun would still reach the sanctuary on 22 February and 22 October
claims.quote: The temples were oriented at the new location to duplicate the two occasions each year that the rising sun penetrated the innermost sanctum at the rear of the Great Temple.

claims.claim: The dates are said to be the king's birthday and coronation day, with no direct evidence
claims.quote: These dates are allegedly the king's birthday and coronation day, respectively. There is no direct evidence to support this.

claims.claim: Earth's axial precession means the original date was different when the temple was built
claims.quote: Because of the accumulated drift of the Tropic of Cancer due to Earth's axial precession over the past 3 millennia, the event's date must have been different when the temple was built.
